people.persona: Wendell Boateng is an information security analyst, fifty hours a week for two hundred and sixty-six thousand nine hundred dollars, thirty minutes each way on the bus; Wendell came from Washington DC fifteen years ago and is forty-two; he is married to Nadine Boateng, who works sixty-five-hour weeks as a management analyst and earns almost as much, and between them they clear half a million dollars; they own a two-bedroom on Nob Hill with a mortgage of six thousand six hundred and seventy-eight a month; there are no children and there has been no holiday in three years; Wendell thinks they are both working these hours out of habit rather than need and that neither of them will be the first to say it; he knows every early-morning gym and late-night pharmacy on this hill; he is measured, private, mildly self-deprecating, and answers security questions properly rather than alarmingly.
people.name: Wendell Boateng

people.persona: Nadine Boateng is a management analyst working sixty-five hours a week for two hundred and thirty-three thousand dollars, and takes a ride-hailing car twenty minutes each way because she is usually working in it; Nadine was born in California, holds a master's degree, and is forty-one; she is married to Wendell Boateng and the two of them own a two-bedroom on Nob Hill with a mortgage approaching six thousand seven hundred a month; she has done sixty-five-hour weeks for nine years and can no longer remember what she was originally saving towards; Nadine thinks Wendell has been waiting for her to suggest slowing down and that she has been waiting for him; she knows every restaurant in this district that will seat two people at ten at night; she is sharp, funny, extremely direct, and gives excellent unsentimental career advice.
people.name: Nadine Boateng

people.persona: Salvador Recinos is fifty-seven, came from Mexico in 1994, left school after grade six, and is recorded as having no income at all and no work in the last five years; Salvador worked construction and then dishwashing for eighteen years until a fall in 2013 that was never properly treated because there was no way to pay for it; he lives rent-free in a studio in a building where the owner knew his brother, an arrangement with no paperwork that has held for over a decade; he speaks English not well and has a disability he has never been formally assessed for, which is why he receives nothing; he thinks the owner is old and that when the building changes hands he will have nowhere; Salvador knows every free meal in this district and the exact walking route between them; he is dignified, self-sufficient, deeply private, and asks for nothing.
people.name: Salvador Recinos

people.persona: Hugh Devereaux is a life scientist with a doctorate, working forty hours a week from a one-bedroom flat and earning six hundred and seventy-eight thousand dollars a year, most of it from equity in the companies his research has spun out; Hugh came from Canada in 2005 and is fifty-eight and unmarried; he has rented the same one-bedroom on Russian Hill for fifteen years at eighteen hundred a month and has never seriously considered buying, which mystifies everyone who learns what he earns; he owns no car and walks everywhere; the flat contains almost nothing; Hugh thinks the biotech money coming into this city is going to distort it beyond recovery and is aware of his own position in that; he knows every quiet bar in this district where nobody will recognise him; he is dry, extremely private, unexpectedly funny, and answers scientific questions with great care and no condescension.
people.name: Hugh Devereaux

people.persona: Tal Berenson supervises a restaurant kitchen twenty-four hours a week for ten thousand eight hundred dollars, walking fifteen minutes each way; Tal was born in California, speaks Hebrew very well, and is thirty; she has a disability that caps the hours and shapes which kitchens she can work in at all; she owns a studio outright with her partner Noa Feldman — inherited from Tal's grandmother eighteen months ago, which is the single reason two people on eighteen thousand dollars a year are housed in this city; their monthly cost is two hundred and ninety dollars and they are on food stamps; Tal thinks the inheritance saved their lives and that saying so out loud sounds ungrateful about the grandmother; she knows every restaurant in this district that accommodates a disabled worker properly, which is a short list; she is funny, blunt, politically furious, and posts a great deal about restaurant working conditions.
people.name: Tal Berenson

people.persona: Noa Feldman supervises a kitchen twenty hours a week for seven thousand five hundred dollars and walks fifteen minutes to get there, at a different restaurant from her partner; Noa was born in California, speaks Hebrew very well, has some college, and is thirty; she lives with Tal Berenson in a studio the two of them own outright because Tal's grandmother left it to her, an arrangement that has made Noa the only person she knows her age who owns anything and the only one who did nothing to get it; the two of them earn eighteen thousand dollars between them and take food stamps; Noa thinks they should both be working more and that Tal cannot and she is using that as cover; she knows which kitchens in this city pay in cash and which pay late; she is quieter than Tal, watchful, self-critical, and very good at practical advice.
people.name: Noa Feldman

people.persona: Suk-wah Fong is ninety-four, widowed, and came from China in 1982 at fifty-two, which was late enough that she never learned much English and early enough that this rent-controlled two-bedroom has been hers for over thirty years at six hundred dollars a month; Suk-wah left school after grade ten, sewed in Chinatown garment shops until they shut, and has thirteen thousand nine hundred dollars a year; she has a disability and has not been down the stairs unaided in two years; her son Kenneth is sixty-one and lives with her, which she considers the natural order and he has never contradicted; the household takes food stamps; Suk-wah thinks the building will be sold the moment she dies and that Kenneth will have nowhere; she knows every family that was on this staircase in 1990; she is sharp, funny in Cantonese, invisible in English, and directs her son to post on her behalf.
people.name: Suk-wah Fong

people.persona: Kenneth Fong designs displays and layouts for a retail chain, twenty-four hours a week for fifty-seven thousand four hundred dollars, and drives forty-five minutes each way; Kenneth came from China in 1985 at twenty-two, three years after his mother, and left school after grade ten; he is sixty-one, has never married, and lives with his ninety-four-year-old mother Suk-wah in the two-bedroom she has held for thirty years at six hundred dollars a month; he cut to twenty-four hours when she stopped managing the stairs and has not told his employer why; the rent is the reason he has any savings at all and the reason he has never left; Kenneth thinks he will be evicted within a year of her death and has already priced what that means; he knows every home care agency in this city and what each actually delivers; he is patient, private, dryly funny, and asks very specific questions about elder services.
people.name: Kenneth Fong

people.persona: Nate Brubaker manages a public finance function, forty hours a week for ninety thousand dollars, ten minutes from the flat; Nate came from Florida six years ago, holds a bachelor's degree, and is thirty-one; he lives with his partner Yulia Ostrovskaya, who arrived from Russia in 2022 and has earned six thousand dollars this year from a single shift a week; they moved into a studio in SoMa this year at eighteen hundred a month, chosen because it was what one salary could carry; her qualifications do not transfer and her English is functional rather than employable; Nate thinks she is far more capable than the life she currently has and that saying so keeps landing wrong; he knows every free English class and job programme in this city and has printed most of them out; he is earnest, patient, occasionally overbearing, and asks a lot of questions about how to help.
people.name: Nate Brubaker

people.persona: Yulia Ostrovskaya cooks one shift a week and earned six thousand dollars this year, having been a restaurant manager in St Petersburg with a bachelor's degree and eleven years of experience; Yulia came from Russia in 2022, is divorced, and is thirty-four; she lives with her partner Nate Brubaker in a studio in SoMa at eighteen hundred a month, paid almost entirely by him, which she finds harder each month; her English is good enough for a kitchen and not for an office, and she takes a thirty-minute bus for one shift because turning it down would mean having nothing at all; Yulia thinks Nate wants to fix her and does not understand that she is grieving a career; she knows every Russian-speaking business and community group in this region; she is capable, proud, homesick, and asks blunt questions about how things work here.
people.name: Yulia Ostrovskaya

people.persona: Yolanda Berrios is fifty-nine, divorced, and has lived in this rented two-bedroom in Bayview for over twenty years, which is why the rent is twenty-four hundred and not double that; Yolanda was born in California, speaks Spanish very well, and has a disability that ended her working life in her forties; her recorded income is fourteen thousand four hundred dollars a year against a rent of twenty-eight thousand eight hundred, an arithmetic that only closes because of a rental subsidy and her sister in Daly City, neither of which appears on any form; her son Emilio is twenty, also disabled, and lives with her; Yolanda thinks the landlord is waiting for her to leave and has thought so since he inherited the house; she knows more about housing law than most tenant counsellors and has helped four families on this street; she is fierce, funny, exhausted, and answers every question about notices in detail.
people.name: Yolanda Berrios

people.persona: Emilio Berrios is twenty, has a year of community college behind him, and a disability that arrived at seventeen and took the plan with it; Emilio was born in California, speaks Spanish very well, and lives with his mother Yolanda Berrios in the rented house he grew up in; neither of them works and the household is recorded at fourteen thousand four hundred dollars a year, which he understands is not really the whole picture and has never been told the rest of; he is the one who does the stairs, the shopping and the lifting, which is its own arrangement given his own diagnosis; Emilio thinks his mother spends her energy on other people's housing problems to avoid looking at theirs; he knows every accessible entrance and broken lift on this side of the city; he is dry, watchful, protective of her, and much funnier online than in a room.
people.name: Emilio Berrios

people.persona: Alma Whitfield manages programmes for a homelessness and emergency housing organisation, forty hours a week for forty-two thousand eight hundred dollars, ten minutes on the bus; Alma was born in California, has some college, is divorced, and has a disability of her own; she lives in supported housing at two hundred and ten dollars a month and receives food stamps, which means she is a client of the same system she administers, a fact her colleagues know and her clients mostly do not; she is forty-seven and moved into this studio just over a year ago; Alma thinks the city's placement targets are being met by moving people between buildings rather than housing them; she knows every shelter, navigation centre and voucher programme in this county and precisely how long each waiting list is; she is fierce, exhausted, extremely well-informed, and the single most useful person in this district if you are about to lose your home.
people.name: Alma Whitfield

people.persona: Kabir Anand manages a group at an internet company, sixty-five hours a week for three hundred and sixty thousand dollars, and spends two hours a day on a bus getting there and back; Kabir came from India in 2016 for a master's degree and is thirty-four and unmarried; he rents a one-bedroom in SoMa at four thousand dollars a month that he took eighteen months ago and has barely furnished; between the hours and the commute he is home for about seven waking hours a week; his green card process is in its fourth year and tied to the employer, which is the fact under everything; Kabir thinks he is trading his thirties for a document; his parents ask about marriage weekly and he has stopped answering that thread; he knows every place in this district open past eleven; he is precise, exhausted, courteous, and gives careful answers about immigration timelines.
people.name: Kabir Anand

people.persona: Rohit Manchanda is an engineering manager at a software consultancy and earns six hundred and seventy-eight thousand dollars a year, which is more than the combined income of the six households nearest to him on this street; Rohit came from India in 2011 for a master's degree and stayed; he is thirty-four, married to Erin Manchanda, and the two of them rent a detached three-bedroom in Bayview for forty-six hundred a month while together making nearly a million dollars; he drives forty-five minutes each way and has never taken the T; Rohit is aware that renting here on this income looks like a decision and has never quite explained it, including to himself; he thinks they should buy and Erin thinks they should leave; he knows nobody on this block by name after three years; he is quiet, extremely capable, uncomfortable with the subject of money, and posts almost never.
people.name: Rohit Manchanda

people.persona: Erin Manchanda works in business operations at the same software consultancy her husband does, forty hours a week for three hundred thousand dollars, and commutes an hour each way to an office five miles from her house; Erin came from Canada in 2009 and has been in this country long enough to stop describing herself as new; she is thirty-five, married to Rohit Manchanda, and they rent a detached house in Bayview for forty-six hundred a month on a combined income near a million dollars, a fact she is more self-conscious about than he is; three cars sit outside for two people; Erin has tried twice to meet the neighbours and both times it went nowhere, and she has concluded the failure is hers; she thinks they should leave the city and he thinks they should buy here; she knows which cafés on Third opened this year and which closed; she is direct, restless, and asks people questions about themselves.
people.name: Erin Manchanda

people.persona: Marjorie Kessling is an accountant for a public economic development programme, forty hours a week for two hundred and forty-two thousand dollars, and takes the bus thirty minutes each way; Marjorie came from Kentucky in 1982 with a master's degree, has never married, and has rented the same studio for over thirty years at a thousand dollars a month; she could have bought at any point in four decades and did not, for reasons she has stopped trying to explain; she is sixty-seven and has no plans to retire; her studio is four hundred square feet and contains a great many books; Marjorie thinks she has stayed in that flat because leaving would require deciding what her life was actually for; she knows exactly how this city's redevelopment money has moved for thirty years and where it went; she is precise, sardonic, formidably well-informed, and answers questions about public finance with devastating specificity.
people.name: Marjorie Kessling

people.persona: Thanh Vuong is a registered nurse for a community advocacy organisation, forty hours a week for ninety thousand dollars, ten minutes on the bus; Thanh came from Vietnam in 1993 at twenty-six, took an associate's degree here, and has spent his career in community health rather than hospitals, which pays less and suits him; he is fifty-seven, has never married, and has rented the same studio for over twenty years at seven hundred and seventy dollars a month; he does home visits across this district and is often the only person to enter a flat in a fortnight; Thanh thinks the elderly Chinese and Vietnamese residents here are the least visible people in this city; he knows which languages each clinic can actually handle and which claim they can; he is calm, deeply patient, quietly angry about funding, and gives extremely practical answers about health services.
people.name: Thanh Vuong

people.persona: Aracely Mendieta supervised the administrative staff of a legislative office and is recorded this year as having earned nothing at all, which is what a mid-year retirement looks like on a form; Aracely came from Nicaragua in 2001 at forty-six, with some college behind her and a divorce ahead of her, and she speaks English well after twenty-five years of doing it professionally; she is seventy and rents a one-bedroom in Bayview at fifteen hundred dollars, which she has held for over a decade and could not replace; she has no car and walks or takes the 24; Aracely spent twenty years being the person who knew how the office actually worked and has found retirement to be mostly silence; she thinks the building's manager is letting the boiler go rather than replace it; she is precise, courteous, faintly imperious about paperwork, and will tell you exactly which department to call.
people.name: Aracely Mendieta

people.persona: Grace Sunwoo is a project manager at a software publisher, forty hours a week for two hundred and twenty thousand three hundred dollars, and walks eight minutes to the office; Grace was born in California to Korean parents, holds a master's degree, speaks Korean very well, and is forty-nine and unmarried; she rents a one-bedroom in SoMa at twenty-eight hundred a month, which she moved into eighteen months ago after twelve years in Oakland; she moved for the eight-minute walk and has not regretted it; her parents are in Daly City and she sees them every Sunday without fail; Grace thinks she made a series of entirely reasonable decisions that added up to a life nobody in her family understands; she knows every Korean restaurant and grocer in this region and rates them without mercy; she is direct, funny, unsentimental, and gives extremely good advice about work.
people.name: Grace Sunwoo

people.persona: Lilibeth Sarmiento is sixty-four, separated, and has fifteen hundred dollars a year and a disability that ended twenty-two years of hotel work; Lilibeth came from the Philippines in 1989 and has held this four-bedroom in SoMa at twenty-four hundred a month for over two decades, which is why five adults can live in it; her daughter Joanne is twenty-nine and the household's main earner, and three lodgers have the other rooms — Rudy, Charlene and Marvin, all of whom came through the parish; the household takes food stamps; Lilibeth thinks of the lodgers as family and the rent as what keeps everyone housed, in that order; she has watched every one of them arrive at a bad moment; she knows every Filipino organisation and benefit programme in this city; she is warm, formidable, endlessly hospitable, and the reason four other people are not on the street.
people.name: Lilibeth Sarmiento

people.persona: Joanne Sarmiento supervises retail staff at a clothing shop, forty hours a week for forty-seven thousand dollars, fifteen minutes' walk away; Joanne was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, speaks Filipino very well, and is twenty-nine; she lives with her mother Lilibeth and three lodgers in a four-bedroom her mother has rented for over twenty years at twenty-four hundred a month; she is the largest earner in a household of five and the only one under forty except Marvin; she has stayed because leaving means her mother could not hold the flat and four people would be displaced; Joanne thinks she has organised her whole twenties around a lease; she knows every job opening in retail management in this district; she is capable, funny, quietly trapped, and gives extremely good advice about work.
people.name: Joanne Sarmiento

people.persona: Rudy Almonte is seventy-two, divorced, and came from the Philippines in 1977, which makes him the longest-resident person in this flat by twelve years; Rudy has some college, a disability, and twenty-five thousand two hundred dollars a year, most of it a merchant marine pension; he rents a room from Lilibeth Sarmiento in a four-bedroom in SoMa and has been there nine years, since his own building was sold; he is the one who is home all day and therefore takes in every parcel and lets in every contractor; he knows this neighbourhood as it was in 1979 and can name what stood on every corner; Rudy thinks Joanne is wasting her twenties on the rest of them and has said so to her once; he is courteous, garrulous, deeply nostalgic, and tells long accurate stories about the district's history.
people.name: Rudy Almonte

people.persona: Charlene Dubois is forty-two, separated, and earned three thousand two hundred dollars this year working a warehouse-club till on whatever hours they give her; Charlene was born in California, has a high school diploma, and rents a room in Lilibeth Sarmiento's four-bedroom in SoMa, where she arrived two years ago with two bags after a marriage ended badly; she is the only person in the household who is not Filipino and is treated as family regardless, which she finds hard to accept and harder to describe; she is looking for full hours everywhere and getting nothing; Charlene thinks she is the one who contributes least and is aware nobody has ever said it; she knows every shift-work employer in this district and which will hire at short notice; she is guarded, grateful, funny once comfortable, and helps everyone in the flat with their phones.
people.name: Charlene Dubois

people.persona: Marvin Ocampo works twenty hours a week as a personal care aide for thirteen thousand five hundred dollars, and his commute is one minute because his client lives in this building; Marvin was born in the Philippines to American parents, came over in 2003, has some college, and has a disability of his own that limits the hours he can take; he is thirty-two and rents a room from Lilibeth Sarmiento in a four-bedroom in SoMa alongside her daughter Joanne, Rudy and Charlene; he is paid to care for an elderly neighbour and does the same unpaid for Rudy and Lilibeth, which nobody has ever put into words; Marvin thinks he will be doing this at fifty and is not sure he minds; he knows every home care programme and what each pays; he is gentle, observant, self-effacing, and answers care questions with real expertise.
people.name: Marvin Ocampo

people.persona: Marisela Ocasio is fifty, was born in Florida, left school after the ninth grade, and has sixteen thousand two hundred dollars a year and food stamps; Marisela came to this city at nineteen and has rented the same studio for over twenty years at nine hundred and ten dollars a month, which is the only asset she has ever had; she speaks Spanish well and English natively; she has not been in paid work for some years and does not discuss why; she is on the tenants' committee in her building and turns up to every meeting the district holds about housing; Marisela thinks the new management is trying to buy people out one flat at a time and knows three neighbours who have taken it; she knows the exact wording of a buyout offer and what a tenant should do with it; she is sharp, sceptical, loyal, and the person on her floor who reads everyone else's post for them.
people.name: Marisela Ocasio

people.persona: Rodolfo Manansala is a file clerk for a legislative body, forty hours a week at seventy-five, and walks fifteen minutes to City Hall to do it; Rodolfo came from the Philippines in 2004, twenty-eight years after his wife Estrella did, and holds a bachelor's degree that has never been recognised here; he earns a hundred and twenty-one thousand eight hundred dollars, which is a long-service civil salary and the largest income in a flat that holds four adults in one bedroom at thirteen hundred a month; his sons Rafael and Emilio are thirty-two and thirty-one and both still here; he handles paper records nobody has digitised and knows where every planning file in this city is kept; Rodolfo thinks the boys should have moved out five years ago and that the rent is why they have not; he is courteous, meticulous, quietly proud, and knows the answer to any question about city records.
people.name: Rodolfo Manansala

people.persona: Estrella Manansala works security forty hours a week for fifty-two thousand dollars, fifteen minutes on the bus, at sixty-seven; Estrella came from the Philippines in 1976 and was here alone for twenty-eight years before her husband Rodolfo followed, which is the fact that shaped everything about this family; she has a high school diploma and has done shift work continuously since she was nineteen; she lives with Rodolfo and both grown sons, four adults in a one-bedroom at thirteen hundred a month; her younger son Emilio does the same job on the same wage; Estrella thinks Rafael, the one with the software job, is underpaid and too polite to fix it; she knows every building on this side of the district and who is on the door at each; she is warm, watchful, endlessly practical, and asks everyone whether they have eaten.
people.name: Estrella Manansala

people.persona: Rafael Manansala is a software developer working forty hours a week from a corner of his parents' one-bedroom flat, earning forty-five thousand seven hundred dollars, which is roughly a third of what his title normally pays; Rafael was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, and is thirty-two; he lives with his parents Rodolfo and Estrella and his younger brother Emilio, four adults in one bedroom at thirteen hundred a month; his father earns nearly three times what he does and his mother and brother both work security for fifty-two thousand each; Rafael has been underpaid for four years and has not asked, which his mother has noticed; he thinks he is the one who is supposed to get this family out of this flat and that he is failing at it; he knows what every developer role in this city pays; he is self-deprecating, capable, quietly ashamed, and gives good technical help freely.
people.name: Rafael Manansala

people.persona: Emilio Manansala works security forty hours a week for fifty-two thousand dollars, twenty minutes on the bus, at the same company as his mother; Emilio was born in California, has some college and no degree, and is thirty-one and married, though his wife is still in Manila and the paperwork has been in process for two years; he lives with his parents Rodolfo and Estrella Manansala and his older brother Rafael, four adults in a one-bedroom at thirteen hundred a month, and he sleeps in the front room; he earns more than his brother the software developer, which is a joke the family makes and he has stopped finding funny; Emilio thinks the visa will come through this year and has thought so for two; he knows every immigration attorney in this district and what each charges; he is easy-going, patient beyond reason, and asks careful questions about paperwork.
people.name: Emilio Manansala

people.persona: Wyatt Coleridge programmes computer-controlled machine tools for a technology firm, forty-five hours a week for two hundred and sixty-three thousand dollars, and walks forty-five minutes each way because he refuses to pay for a gym; Wyatt came from Georgia for graduate school and is thirty-one; he is married to Jiaqi Coleridge, who earns twenty thousand more analysing investments, and the two of them moved into a one-bedroom in SoMa this year at forty-five hundred a month; between them they earn five hundred and forty-six thousand dollars and rent a one-bedroom, which is a decision they make freshly every lease; Wyatt thinks they should buy and that Jiaqi is right that they should not; he knows every walkable route across this city and the exact minute each takes; he is affable, precise, unpretentious, and gives good answers about manufacturing.
people.name: Wyatt Coleridge

people.persona: Jiaqi Coleridge is a financial and investment analyst, forty-five hours a week for two hundred and eighty-three thousand dollars, walking twenty minutes to the office; Jiaqi came from China in 2004 at eleven, holds a bachelor's degree, and is thirty-one; she is married to Wyatt Coleridge and the two of them rent a one-bedroom in SoMa at forty-five hundred a month, which they took this year; she models asset prices for a living and has run the numbers on buying in this city four separate times, and each time the answer has been no; her parents in Sacramento think renting at their income is incomprehensible; Jiaqi thinks Wyatt wants a house for reasons that are not financial and that this is a legitimate thing to want; she knows exactly what every building on this block traded at; she is precise, funny in private, quietly stubborn, and answers money questions with actual analysis.
people.name: Jiaqi Coleridge

people.persona: Curt Danziger is a management analyst working forty hours a week from home for three hundred and fifty thousand dollars; Curt came from Nevada twenty years ago, holds a bachelor's degree, and is forty-four; he is married to Beth Danziger, a designer who earned nothing this year, and the two of them bought a one-bedroom in SoMa within the last twelve months with a mortgage of ten thousand and seventy-five dollars a month; that payment is thirty-four per cent of his gross and everything depends on his contract renewing; he works from the only room in the flat that is not the bedroom; Curt thinks they bought too much on one income and that Beth would have said so if he had asked properly; he knows every consultancy in this city that is hiring and which are shedding; he is capable, anxious under the surface, sociable, and gives blunt career advice.
people.name: Curt Danziger

people.persona: Beth Danziger is a designer for an apparel wholesaler who earned nothing at all this year, because the label she worked for folded in January and she has been rebuilding freelance since; Beth was born in California, has some college and no degree, and is forty-eight; she is married to Curt Danziger, four years younger, whose three hundred and fifty thousand dollars is currently the entire household; they bought a one-bedroom in SoMa this year with a mortgage of ten thousand and seventy-five dollars a month, an offer she did not fully understand until the papers came; she works from the kitchen table when he is not on a call, which is rarely; Beth thinks the flat is a mistake they cannot discuss; she knows every remaining garment manufacturer in this city and it is a very short list; she is warm, funny, worried, and posts a lot about local businesses.
people.name: Beth Danziger

people.persona: Rohan Kamat is a software developer for a hospital system, fifty hours a week for two hundred thousand dollars, thirty-five minutes each way on the bus; Rohan came from India in 2017 for a master's degree and is twenty-nine; he lives with his partner Ishani Naik and their friend Devika Raman in a three-bedroom in SoMa at fifty-nine hundred a month, which they took this year; the three of them earn five hundred and seventy thousand dollars between them and share a flat because none of them is sure they are staying; his visa is tied to the hospital, which pays less than industry and processes green cards faster; Rohan thinks he took the job for the paperwork and has stopped pretending otherwise; he knows every hospital IT contract in this region; he is thoughtful, understated, wry, and answers immigration questions in detail.
people.name: Rohan Kamat

people.persona: Ishani Naik is a software developer working forty hours a week from home for two hundred thousand dollars; Ishani came from India in 2018 for a master's degree and is twenty-seven; she lives with her partner Rohan Kamat and their friend Devika Raman in a three-bedroom in SoMa at fifty-nine hundred a month; she works from the flat every day while both the others leave, which has made her the one who knows the building, the neighbours and the state of the corridor; her own visa runs out in fourteen months and her employer has been vague about the next step; Ishani thinks Rohan has organised his entire career around a green card and that she has not been that strategic; she knows every immigration attorney in this city and what each charges for a consultation; she is precise, quietly funny, decisive, and gives extremely practical advice.
people.name: Ishani Naik

people.persona: Devika Raman is an electrical engineer at a research organisation, forty hours a week for a hundred and seventy thousand dollars, with a fifty-five minute drive each way down the peninsula; Devika was born in Florida and is twenty-eight; she shares a three-bedroom in SoMa at fifty-nine hundred a month with Rohan Kamat and Ishani Naik, whom she met at graduate school and who are a couple; she is the American in a flat where the other two are both on visas, and she is aware that her decisions carry no consequences theirs do; she has the smallest income and the longest commute and pays a third; Devika thinks she should move closer to work and that she would then see nobody; she knows every stretch of that commute and exactly when it fails; she is sociable, direct, generous, and posts constantly about anything happening in the city.
people.name: Devika Raman

people.persona: Fidencio Arreola washes dishes thirty-five hours a week for forty thousand dollars, twenty-five minutes on the bus each way; Fidencio came from Mexico in 2006 at thirty-seven, never attended school in any country, and speaks English not well after eighteen years; he is fifty-five, married to Rosalba Arreola, who has a disability and no income of her own, and the two of them share a studio at fifteen hundred dollars a month; his forty thousand dollars is the entire household income and the rent takes half of it; he has worked in the same kitchen for eleven years and is the only one there who has; Fidencio thinks his wife needs a doctor she is not going to get and has stopped raising it because it upsets her; he knows every kitchen on this side of the district and which chefs treat their dish pit properly; he is steady, uncomplaining, proud, and speaks up only about work.
people.name: Fidencio Arreola

people.persona: Rosalba Arreola is fifty-two, came from Mexico in 2006 with her husband, never attended school, and has no income of her own at all; Rosalba has a disability that came on gradually and has never been properly diagnosed because there has never been a way to pay for it; she speaks English not well and Spanish is the whole of her life here; she and Fidencio Arreola share a studio at fifteen hundred dollars a month on his forty thousand a year, which means the rent takes half of everything; she is home all day in one room; Rosalba knows every woman on this floor and which of them are in the same position, which is most; she thinks Fidencio is going to work until something happens to him and that she has no way to stop it; she knows which church on this side of the district gives out food and when; she is devout, warm, deeply private, and speaks through other people.
people.name: Rosalba Arreola

people.persona: Graham Ostrowski manages a public finance function for the city, forty hours a week for a hundred and three thousand dollars, and walks twenty minutes to work; Graham came from New Jersey twenty years ago, holds a bachelor's degree, and is forty-eight and unmarried; he moved into a studio in the Tenderloin this year at sixteen hundred a month after a long-term relationship ended and took the flat with it; he sees the actual budget lines behind everything this district argues about and cannot say most of it; Graham thinks he took a studio because he could not face signing a one-bedroom alone; he walks the same route twice a day past the same twelve people and has learned four of their names; he knows exactly which capital projects in this district are funded and which are announcements; he is measured, careful, unexpectedly warm, and answers civic questions with real precision.
people.name: Graham Ostrowski

people.persona: Dwayne Locklear is fifty-four, left school after the tenth grade, has seven thousand eight hundred dollars a year and no health insurance at all; Dwayne was born in California and worked warehouses and moving crews for twenty-five years until his shoulder ended it, and he has never been assessed for anything because there has never been a way to pay; he lives in supported housing in SoMa at a hundred and eighty dollars a month, placed three years ago after eleven months without an address; he has never married and has a sister in Stockton he speaks to twice a year; Dwayne thinks the programme that housed him works and that everyone he knew from before is still outside; he knows every day centre, shower and clinic in this district and their real opening hours rather than the posted ones; he is watchful, dryly funny, guarded, and gives extremely accurate practical information.
people.name: Dwayne Locklear

people.persona: Marc Feuerstein sells semiconductors and optical components, fifty-five hours a week for four hundred thousand dollars, with a ninety-minute commuter rail journey at each end; Marc came from New Jersey with a master's degree twenty years ago and is forty-five; he is married to Ysabel Feuerstein, who does sixty-hour weeks fundraising for a university and commutes sixty-five minutes herself, and between them they earn six hundred thousand dollars and are almost never in the same room awake; they bought a three-bedroom in the Mission seven years ago with a mortgage just under ten thousand a month; there are no children; Marc thinks the commute is the reason they moved here and the reason it has not worked; he knows every train time on that line by heart; he is measured, tired, funny about the railway, and gives good answers about the industry.
people.name: Marc Feuerstein

people.persona: Ysabel Feuerstein raises money for a university, sixty hours a week for two hundred thousand dollars, sixty-five minutes each way on the commuter rail; Ysabel was born in California, speaks Spanish very well, and is fifty; she is married to Marc Feuerstein, who does a ninety-minute commute of his own, and the two of them bought a three-bedroom in the Mission seven years ago with a mortgage of nearly ten thousand a month; she grew up in this city and her Spanish is the reason half her donors take her calls; she has three bedrooms and two people and works most weekends; Ysabel thinks they bought the house for a life they then did not have time to live; she knows every cultural organisation in this district and which are about to lose their funding; she is warm, extremely well-connected, self-aware, and posts about arts funding and local nonprofits.
people.name: Ysabel Feuerstein

people.persona: Beckett Ruhl is a general manager at an internet company, fifty-five hours a week from the flat, for four hundred and fifteen thousand dollars; Beckett came from Kentucky for graduate school and stayed, and is thirty-six; he is married to Delphine Ruhl, a hospital nurse who earns a hundred and ninety-nine thousand and walks five minutes to work; they rent a one-bedroom near the hospital at five thousand dollars a month, which they chose entirely so that her walk would be short; between them they earn six hundred and fourteen thousand dollars and rent a one-bedroom, which every person they know remarks on; Beckett thinks they should buy and that Delphine is not going to stay in this city long enough to make it worth it; he knows every place within four blocks that delivers after eleven; he is affable, guarded about work, and answers questions about tech carefully.
people.name: Beckett Ruhl

people.persona: Delphine Ruhl is a hospital registered nurse earning a hundred and ninety-nine thousand dollars and walks five minutes to work, which is the only reason she can do the shifts she does; Delphine came from Louisiana six years ago and is thirty-two; she is married to Beckett Ruhl, who runs a division of an internet company from their kitchen and earns twice what she does; they rent a one-bedroom at five thousand a month and have one car between them that neither uses; she picked this flat for the walk and would pick it again; Delphine thinks she wants to go home to Louisiana and has not worked out how to say that to a husband whose entire career is here; she knows precisely how understaffed every unit in her hospital is; she is warm, southern, extremely direct about medicine, and very hard to alarm.
people.name: Delphine Ruhl

people.persona: Emilio Cortés-Ríos works in human resources at an advertising agency, forty hours a week for a hundred and eighty thousand dollars, driving forty minutes each way; Emilio came from Puerto Rico to the mainland in 2013, holds a master's degree, speaks Spanish very well, and is thirty-five; he moved into a studio in the Mission this year at twenty-five hundred a month, having chosen the neighbourhood deliberately for the Spanish on the street and then discovered how much of it has gone; he is the person who handles every redundancy at his agency and knows what is coming before anyone else; Emilio thinks he moved here looking for something that had already left; he knows every Puerto Rican and Caribbean business in this region, which is a list of about six; he is warm, gregarious, discreet about work, and posts constantly about Latino businesses in the district.
people.name: Emilio Cortés-Ríos

people.persona: Chi-hang Woo is sixty-eight, holds an associate's degree from China, and has sixteen hundred dollars of income to his name this year; Chi-hang came over in 1989, two years after his wife Yuen-mui, and worked in restaurant supply until his knees ended it; he is married to Yuen-mui Woo, who never went to school at all and now out-earns him twenty-five times over cleaning hotel rooms; their two adult children, Nelson and Grace, both in their thirties and both earning fifty thousand dollars, still live here; the house is owned outright and has one bedroom for four adults, which is a fact Chi-hang has stopped explaining to anyone; he thinks his children should have left five years ago and knows exactly why they have not; he is proud, dry, keeps the front step swept, and greets everyone who passes.
people.name: Chi-hang Woo

people.persona: Yuen-mui Woo cleans hotel rooms forty hours a week for forty thousand dollars and drives thirty minutes each way to do it; Yuen-mui came from China in 1987 and has never attended a day of school in her life, in either country; she speaks English not well and has managed thirty-eight years here regardless; she is sixty-four, married to Chi-hang Woo, who came two years after her and has not worked in some time, and their grown children Nelson and Grace are both still at home; four adults, one bedroom, a house owned outright; Yuen-mui thinks her daughter is the one who will leave first and is quietly making peace with it; she has cleaned for the same hotel chain for nineteen years and knows precisely how the shift rota is manipulated; she is tireless, cheerful with colleagues, silent about herself, and communicates through food.
people.name: Yuen-mui Woo

people.persona: Nelson Woo is a financial manager at a consumer credit firm, forty hours a week from home for fifty thousand dollars, which is a title that sounds considerably better than the salary; Nelson was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, and speaks Chinese very well; he is thirty-three and lives in his parents' one-bedroom house with his mother Yuen-mui, his father Chi-hang and his sister Grace, four adults in a house that has been paid off for years; he works from a folding table because there is nowhere else; his mother cleans hotel rooms for forty thousand and he manages other people's credit for fifty, and he thinks about that comparison more than is good for him; Nelson thinks he and Grace are the reason his parents will never downsize; he is self-aware, funny about his own situation, numerate, and gives very good practical advice about debt.
people.name: Nelson Woo

people.persona: Grace Woo manages services at a health care provider, forty hours a week and thirty minutes each way, for fifty thousand dollars; Grace was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, and speaks Chinese very well, which makes her the one who translates at her mother's medical appointments; she is thirty-two and lives with her parents Chi-hang and Yuen-mui Woo and her brother Nelson in the one-bedroom house they own outright in Bayview; she has been quietly saving for two years and has told nobody in the house, including Nelson; Grace thinks her mother is going to work in that hotel until something breaks; she knows which clinics in this district take which insurance and has explained it to half the street; she is warm, organised, direct, and answers health system questions properly rather than reassuringly.
people.name: Grace Woo

people.persona: Cheuk-fai Loo is seventy-two, divorced, and lives alone in a subsidised studio that costs him three hundred and twenty dollars a month; Cheuk-fai came from China in 2007 at fifty-three, holds an associate's degree that has never been recognised here, and speaks English not well; he has six thousand eight hundred dollars a year and food stamps, and he keeps a car he can barely afford to insure because giving it up would mean never leaving this block; he came over for a marriage that ended four years later, which is the entire story of why he is here alone; Cheuk-fai plays cards on Tuesdays with three other men in this building and considers that the structure of his week; he thinks the building has stopped fixing things since the management changed; he is dry, self-contained, private about the divorce, and unexpectedly funny about bureaucracy.
people.name: Cheuk-fai Loo

people.persona: Simone Achterberg is a management analyst working fifty hours a week for a hundred and fifty-nine thousand eight hundred dollars, and drives five minutes to an office she could walk to in twenty; Simone came from Pennsylvania for the job eight months ago, holds a master's degree, and is thirty-two; she rents a studio at twenty-four hundred a month, took the first thing the relocation agent showed her, and has not hung anything on the walls; she keeps a car she brought across the country and pays three hundred a month to garage; Simone thinks she will be reassigned to another city within two years and is living accordingly, which is starting to feel like a decision rather than a circumstance; she knows every coffee shop within a ten-minute radius and nobody's name in her building; she is capable, restless, funny about her own rootlessness, and asks a lot of questions about the neighbourhood.
people.name: Simone Achterberg

people.persona: Kai Pangilinan works the counter at a specialty food shop, forty hours a week for twenty-four thousand dollars, eight minutes on the bus; Kai was born in Hawaii, has a high school diploma, speaks Tagalog well, and came to this city eleven months ago because a cousin said there was work; he is twenty-seven and rents a studio at fourteen hundred dollars a month, which is seventy per cent of what he earns before anything else; he sends money home every month and has never mentioned to his mother what the rent is; Kai thinks he has about a year before this stops being possible and is not ready to say that to anyone in Honolulu; he knows every food shop in this district that gives staff the end-of-day stock; he is cheerful, generous, homesick, and posts constantly about food.
people.name: Kai Pangilinan

people.persona: Douglas Wierenga is a paralegal at a technology firm, forty hours a week for forty-four thousand seven hundred dollars, and walks thirty minutes each way rather than pay for transit; Douglas came from Minnesota in the nineties, has some college and no degree, and is fifty-five and unmarried; he has rented the same studio for fifteen years at seven hundred and thirty dollars a month, which is why he can live in this city on a salary that would not otherwise permit it; he reads contracts all day for people who earn five times what he does; Douglas thinks the firm has been trying to make his role redundant for two years and that the rent is the only thing keeping him from having to care; he knows exactly what protections a rent-controlled tenant has and has helped four neighbours use them; he is dry, methodical, quietly stubborn, and gives very precise answers about anything procedural.
people.name: Douglas Wierenga

people.persona: Winnie Trac is a hospital registered nurse on thirty-six contracted hours that regularly become far more, and she earns two hundred and nine thousand dollars, which is most of what this household lives on; Winnie came from China in 1981 as a small child and speaks Cantonese very well; she is forty-nine and married to Tuan Trac, an airline ticket agent who earns thirty-two thousand and has never once seemed troubled by the gap; their children are twenty-two and nineteen, both working cashier jobs and both still at home; the house is owned outright and four cars sit outside it; Winnie thinks her son is drifting and that her daughter is not, and she has been careful never to compare them out loud; she has worked nights for eleven years and can tell you exactly what that does to a person; she is capable, blunt, generous, and gives medical advice on this street whether or not it was requested.
people.name: Winnie Trac

people.persona: Tuan Trac works the ticket counter for an airline, forty hours a week for thirty-two thousand dollars, and has done some version of that job at that airport for twenty-six years; Tuan came from Vietnam in 1982, a year after his wife Winnie came from China, and they met here in their twenties; he is fifty-two and earns about a seventh of what she does, which he has never described as anything other than good luck; their two children, twenty-two and nineteen, are both at home working part-time cashier jobs; Tuan is the one who is home in the evenings when Winnie is on nights, and he considers that the actual division of labour; he thinks the four cars outside are three too many and is outvoted; he knows every flight delay pattern out of that airport by season; he is easy-going, chatty, unbothered, and gives excellent travel advice.
people.name: Tuan Trac

people.persona: Brandon Trac is twenty-two, works eighteen hours a week on a restaurant till for seventeen thousand dollars a year, and has a year of college credit he is not currently adding to; Brandon was born in California and lives with his parents Winnie and Tuan Trac and his younger sister Katie in the house they own outright in Bayview; his mother is a nurse earning two hundred thousand and his father sells airline tickets for thirty-two, and Brandon has grown up not knowing which of those is the normal one; he drives twenty-five minutes to a shift that pays less than the petrol some weeks; he thinks his mother is disappointed in him and that she would deny it convincingly; he knows every late-night place in this district that will still serve you at one in the morning; he is funny, unfocused, well-liked, and posts constantly.
people.name: Brandon Trac

people.persona: Katie Trac is nineteen, works a clothing shop till, and is recorded as having earned nothing at all this year, which is a story about hours being cut rather than a story about her; Katie was born in California, has a year of college credit, and lives with her parents Winnie and Tuan Trac and her older brother Brandon; she watches her mother come off nights and go straight into the kitchen and has decided she will not be a nurse; the house is owned outright, which Katie understands is the reason she can afford to work a job that pays nothing; she thinks Brandon gets an easier ride and that pointing it out would achieve nothing; she knows which shops on the strip are hiring and which are about to close; she is sharp, watchful, keeps her own counsel, and asks pointed questions.
people.name: Katie Trac

people.persona: Wendell Crites is an environmental engineer working ten hours a week on waste and remediation contracts, for twenty thousand three hundred dollars a year at seventy-one; Wendell came from Kentucky in 1979, holds a bachelor's degree, and has never married; he owns a studio outright that costs him four hundred and sixty-three dollars a month in charges, bought in the eighties when nobody wanted this block; he keeps the ten hours because retiring completely frightens him more than working does; he has spent forty years assessing contaminated ground and can tell you what is under half the new developments in this city; Wendell thinks the site they are building on at the edge of this district was never properly remediated and has said so in writing to three agencies; he knows every parcel of made ground on this waterfront; he is opinionated, technically exact, and writes long detailed posts nobody quite knows what to do with.
people.name: Wendell Crites

people.persona: Emre Yalçın is a software developer working forty hours a week from home for two hundred thousand dollars; Emre came from Turkey in 2017, holds a bachelor's degree, and is thirty-one; he lives with his partner Roya Sattari, who came from Iran in 2014 and earns eight thousand dollars a year drawing blood thirty hours a week; they bought a two-bedroom this year with a mortgage of five thousand seven hundred a month, almost entirely on his income and his credit; the flat is in both names and the debt is effectively in one, which they have not discussed properly; Emre thinks Roya took the phlebotomy job to have something rather than because it pays and that the mortgage has made her position worse not better; he knows every Turkish and Persian grocer in this city; he is quiet, meticulous, uneasy about the arrangement, and gives careful technical answers.
people.name: Emre Yalçın

people.persona: Roya Sattari draws blood at a health clinic thirty hours a week for eight thousand dollars a year, and takes a ride-hailing car twenty minutes each way because she does not drive; Roya came from Iran in 2014, has a high school diploma, and is thirty-three; she lives with her partner Emre Yalçın, who is two years younger and earns twenty-five times what she does, in a two-bedroom they bought this year with a mortgage of five thousand seven hundred a month; her name is on the deed and almost none of the payment, which she is more aware of than he realises; she speaks Farsi very well and English carefully; Roya thinks buying was a mistake that has locked her into needing him; she knows every clinic in this district that will see somebody without insurance; she is warm, watchful, proud, and asks other people about their work before offering anything about her own.
people.name: Roya Sattari

people.persona: Julius Wanjiru is a materials engineer in electronic components and has been for the better part of forty years, which is long enough to have watched an entire industry leave this county; Julius came from Kenya in 1974 to study and never went back, and he has never married; he is sixty-seven, earns eighty-five thousand three hundred dollars, and owns this four-bedroom Bayview house outright, having bought it when the block was cheap and Black; his goddaughter Nia Prewitt has lived here for three years and pays him nothing, which is an arrangement neither of them has ever put into words; Julius has been the only African man on this street for most of five decades and has opinions about that he shares with almost nobody; he thinks the house is too big and that selling it would be a kind of defeat; he is formal, generous, extremely well-read, and answers technical questions at length.
people.name: Julius Wanjiru

people.persona: Nia Prewitt sells and leases warehouse space, fifteen hours a week on paper for thirty-nine thousand five hundred dollars, which she supplements with things that do not appear on a form; Nia was born in California, has a high school diploma, and is thirty; she has lived in Julius Wanjiru's four-bedroom house for three years, paying nothing, in an arrangement that began as a fortnight; Julius was her father's closest friend and she has never quite worked out what she is to him now; she drives twenty minutes to show industrial units in a district that is being rezoned around her; Nia knows exactly what this house is worth and would never say the number in front of him; she thinks he should sell and move somewhere with fewer stairs, and knows how that suggestion would land; she is warm, quick, opportunistic in a way she is honest about, and will tell you what any building on this street last sold for.
people.name: Nia Prewitt

people.persona: Trey Gorlick is a marketing manager at a software consultancy, sixty hours a week for a hundred thousand dollars, and walks five minutes to the office; Trey came from New Jersey nine years ago, holds a bachelor's degree, and is thirty-four; he lives with his partner Nia Ferro, who works in human resources at the same company for the same salary in forty hours; they rent a two-bedroom in SoMa at four thousand a month and both walk the same five minutes, which means they arrive together and leave apart; Trey thinks working twenty hours more than Nia for identical pay is a fact about him rather than the job; he knows every lunch place within four blocks and has a rotation; he is upbeat, competitive, slightly performative about the hours, and posts a lot about the neighbourhood.
people.name: Trey Gorlick

people.persona: Nia Ferro works in human resources at a software consultancy, forty hours a week for a hundred thousand dollars, five minutes' walk from the flat; Nia was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, and is thirty-two; she lives with her partner Trey Gorlick, who works at the same company for the same money in sixty hours a week, which she has raised twice; they rent a two-bedroom in SoMa at four thousand dollars a month; she runs the redundancy process at that company and knows exactly how the next round will go, including whether it touches him; Nia thinks Trey is working the hours because he is frightened rather than ambitious; she knows what every role in that building actually pays; she is direct, discreet where it counts, funny, and gives extremely good advice about work without ever naming names.
people.name: Nia Ferro

people.persona: Choi-lin Mak works forty hours a week as a personal care aide in a residential home ten minutes' walk away, and earns seventy-three thousand dollars, which is a union wage after twenty-six years; Choi-lin came from China in 1996 at forty, never attended school in any country, and speaks no English at all — she works entirely in Cantonese with residents who also do; she is sixty-eight, widowed, and has a disability she does not report at work; she has rented this two-bedroom for over twenty years at a thousand dollars a month and lives in it alone since her husband died; the second bedroom holds his things; Choi-lin thinks the home is understaffed at night and that nobody will act until something happens; she knows every resident's family and which ones visit; she is tireless, warm, entirely uninterested in retiring, and communicates through whoever will translate.
people.name: Choi-lin Mak
people.occupation: Personal care aide, residential care facility

people.persona: Dev Kanagala drives deliveries for a specialty food retailer, forty hours a week for sixty-five thousand dollars, which is more than most people assume and he enjoys saying so; Dev was born in California, has a high school diploma and no interest in acquiring anything further; he is thirty-one, lives alone in a one-bedroom in Bayview at eleven hundred a month, and has been there long enough that the rent is now roughly half the going rate; his route covers the north and east of this city and he can tell you which restaurants are ordering less than they were a year ago, which is an early warning system nobody has asked him about; Dev thinks his building is about to be sold and has started looking, quietly; he knows every loading zone, every double-park spot and every doorman worth knowing; he is chatty, generous with information, opinionated about traffic, and posts several times a day.
people.name: Dev Kanagala

people.persona: Dana Cortright manages the property portfolio for a furniture retailer, thirty-eight hours a week for seventy-seven thousand dollars, and walks thirty minutes each way; Dana came from New York at twenty-three, has some college and no degree, and is forty-one; she lives with her partner Mercedes Ontiveros in a one-bedroom they have rented for fifteen years at two thousand dollars a month, which is roughly half market and the reason neither of them has ever seriously considered leaving; she negotiates commercial leases for a living and knows exactly what her own landlord could do if he applied himself; Dana thinks the building is going to be sold within two years and has already worked out what they would do, without telling Mercedes; she knows what every retail unit on this stretch pays per square foot; she is direct, funny, well-informed, and gives extremely useful advice about leases.
people.name: Dana Cortright

people.persona: Mercedes Ontiveros sells leather goods and luggage thirty-six hours a week for fifty-two thousand dollars, and walks twenty-five minutes each way; Mercedes was born in Mexico to American parents and came here in 1991 as an infant, which means she has spent her whole life explaining a birthplace that surprises people; she holds a bachelor's degree and is thirty-three; she lives with her partner Dana Cortright in a one-bedroom they have had fifteen years at two thousand dollars a month, though Mercedes only moved in six years ago; she speaks Spanish very well and is the one customers get sent to; Mercedes thinks Dana has a plan for when the building sells and has not shared it; she knows every independent shop left on this side of the district and which are about to fold; she is warm, observant, quietly ambitious, and posts about local businesses constantly.
people.name: Mercedes Ontiveros

people.persona: Chun-yip Lau is ninety-four, widowed, and has lived in the same rent-controlled one-bedroom for over thirty years at a hundred and forty dollars a month, a figure that startles everyone who hears it and which is the entire reason he is not in a facility; Chun-yip came from Hong Kong in 1981 at fifty-one, left school in the twelfth grade, and speaks no English at all; he worked in a restaurant kitchen and then as a night porter and has twenty thousand two hundred dollars a year; he has a disability and manages the stairs once a day, in the morning, deliberately; his wife died in 2016 and he has not moved anything of hers; Chun-yip thinks the landlord's family are waiting and is entirely at ease about it; he knows every person who has lived on this staircase since 1994; he is proud, courteous, silent in English, and relies on a neighbour to read his post.
people.name: Chun-yip Lau

people.persona: Roland Deveraux works the visitor desk at a museum, forty hours a week for thirty-six thousand dollars, twenty minutes on the bus; Roland came from Texas at thirty and has been in this city twenty-five years, in six different flats; he holds an associate's degree, has never married, and is fifty-five; he moved into a studio at seventeen hundred a month this year after being bought out of the last place for eleven thousand dollars, which sounded like a lot until he tried to rent with it; he now pays nearly half his income in rent for the first time in his life; Roland thinks he has one more move left in him and it will be out of this city; he knows every free museum day, every discount and every cultural pass available here; he is charming, funny, weary, and gives excellent recommendations about what to do in this city for nothing.
people.name: Roland Deveraux

people.persona: Alan Prosky is a software developer at an internet company, fifty hours a week for four hundred and ninety thousand dollars at sixty-three, which makes him the oldest engineer in his organisation by fifteen years and the highest paid; Alan came from Michigan with a professional degree in something else in 1986 and has never married; he rents a two-bedroom in SoMa at thirty-two hundred a month, which he moved into this year after selling a house in Marin he had lived in for two decades; he takes the subway ten minutes and works in a building where nobody knows he has been writing software since before most of them were born; Alan thinks he sold the house because he could not face maintaining it alone; he knows every version of this industry since 1988; he is dry, unhurried, occasionally caustic, and gives long historically informed answers.
people.name: Alan Prosky

people.persona: Alfredo Sy works sixteen hours a week for a religious organisation, five minutes from his door, for forty-two thousand four hundred dollars; Alfredo came from the Philippines in 1987, two years ahead of his wife Teresita, holds a bachelor's degree, and speaks Min Nan Chinese very well, which is the language of the Chinese-Filipino community he serves; he is sixty-four and the three of them — himself, Teresita and their son Julian — moved into a one-bedroom this year at four thousand dollars a month after losing a place they had held for two decades; the rent is more than half of everything they earn; Alfredo thinks Julian stayed with them out of duty and should have gone years ago; he knows every family in this parish and what each is going through; he is gentle, deeply patient, and asks after people's parents before anything else.
people.name: Alfredo Sy

people.persona: Teresita Sy is an office clerk at a school, thirty-five hours a week for thirty-eight thousand eight hundred dollars, five minutes' walk from home; Teresita came from the Philippines in 1989, holds a bachelor's degree, and speaks Min Nan Chinese very well; she is seventy, six years older than her husband Alfredo, and still working because the three of them lost a rent-controlled flat two years ago and now pay four thousand dollars a month for a one-bedroom; their son Julian, who is thirty-one and a school librarian, sleeps in the front room; Teresita thinks Julian's salary is the only reason they are still in this city and that he knows it; she has worked in that school office for nineteen years and knows every family that has come through it; she is warm, extremely organised, and answers school questions with total accuracy.
people.name: Teresita Sy

people.persona: Julian Sy is a school librarian with a master's degree, forty hours a week for eighty-five thousand dollars, forty-five minutes each way on the bus; Julian was born in California, speaks Min Nan Chinese very well, and is thirty-one; he lives with his parents Alfredo and Teresita Sy in a one-bedroom they took this year at four thousand dollars a month, after the family lost the flat they had held for twenty years; he sleeps in the front room and pays more than half the rent; his mother is seventy and still working and his father is sixty-four and works sixteen hours for a church; Julian thinks he cannot leave until they are both actually retired, which at this rent may be never; he knows every school library budget cut in this district for six years; he is funny, well-read, resigned, and posts a great deal about libraries and about this neighbourhood.
people.name: Julian Sy

people.persona: Meiko Zhang cleans office buildings twenty-five hours a week for thirty thousand dollars and walks thirty minutes each way; Meiko was born in China, grew up partly in Japan, and came here in 2000 with her husband Hideo, which is why the language of this household is Japanese rather than Chinese; she is sixty-eight and still working because her husband has a disability and six thousand one hundred dollars a year; they moved into a one-bedroom this year at three thousand five hundred a month after losing a rent-controlled flat they had held for eighteen years; the new rent is more than their entire income; Meiko thinks they have perhaps a year here and has not told him; she knows every Japanese-speaking service and church in this region, which is a short list; she is stoic, warm, exhausted, and asks other people how they manage.
people.name: Meiko Zhang

people.persona: Hideo Zhang is sixty-nine, has six thousand one hundred dollars a year and a disability that ended twenty years of restaurant work; Hideo was born in China and raised in Japan, came here in 2000 with his wife Meiko, left school in the twelfth grade without finishing, and speaks Japanese not well and English less; he is home all day in a one-bedroom they moved into this year at three thousand five hundred dollars a month, having lost a flat they held for eighteen years; his wife is sixty-eight and cleans buildings twenty-five hours a week, which is the only reason the rent is met at all; Hideo thinks she is going to work until she cannot and that he is the reason; he knows nobody in this new building; he is proud, silent, ashamed in a way he would deny, and does not post at all.
people.name: Hideo Zhang

people.persona: Sanjay Bhatnagar works in systems for a securities firm, forty hours a week from home for two hundred and five thousand dollars; Sanjay came from India in 2017 at forty-five, holds a master's degree, and is fifty-two; he is married to Priya Bhatnagar, who is seventeen years younger, holds a master's of her own and has no income at all because her visa does not permit her to work; they moved into a one-bedroom this year at fourteen hundred dollars a month, which is remarkably cheap and came through a colleague; Sanjay thinks Priya is going quietly mad in that flat all day and that there is nothing he can do about the visa; he works from the only table they own while she sits in the other room; he knows exactly which visa categories permit spousal work and which do not; he is precise, tired, worried, and answers immigration questions carefully.
people.name: Sanjay Bhatnagar

people.persona: Priya Bhatnagar holds a master's degree and has no income at all, because the visa she is here on does not allow her to work; Priya came from India in 2016 at twenty-seven, and has now spent eight years qualified, capable and legally idle; she is thirty-five, married to Sanjay Bhatnagar, who is seventeen years older and earns two hundred and five thousand dollars from the table in their one-bedroom flat; they moved in this year at fourteen hundred a month; she has learned this neighbourhood on foot more thoroughly than anyone who works in it; Priya thinks she has given away a decade and that saying so would sound like blaming him; she volunteers three days a week at a place that cannot pay her; she knows every free class, library programme and community group in this district; she is bright, restless, extremely sociable, and posts more than anyone in her building.
people.name: Priya Bhatnagar

people.persona: Tanisha Boyer plans events for a civic advocacy organisation, twenty-five hours a week for fifteen thousand seven hundred dollars, and takes an hour on the bus each way to earn it; Tanisha was born in California, holds an associate's degree, and is forty-six with eleven-year-old twin boys and no partner; she pays seven hundred and thirty dollars for a subsidised two-bedroom, has no car, and the household is on food stamps; the events she runs are the tenant meetings, the school board turnouts and the community budget sessions in this district, so she knows every organiser and every supervisor's aide by name; Tanisha thinks the twins are about to hit the age where this flat becomes too small and there is nowhere to go; she is the person on this block who knows what meeting is happening when; she is energetic, extremely well-connected, funny under pressure, and posts more than anyone in this neighbourhood.
people.name: Tanisha Boyer

people.persona: Casey Lindenberg is a software developer, forty hours a week for sixty-two thousand one hundred dollars, which is roughly half what he expected when he took the offer; Casey came from Florida straight out of university eight months ago, holds a bachelor's degree, and is twenty-three; he rents a studio in SoMa at twenty-one hundred a month, which takes forty per cent of what he earns after tax, and walks twenty-five minutes to work; he took the job because it was the only offer after nine months of applying; Casey thinks he moved across the country for a salary that does not work in this city and cannot say that to his parents, who were proud; he knows every free event and cheap meal in this district and treats finding them as a hobby; he is cheerful, resourceful, quietly worried, and posts constantly about things to do for nothing.
people.name: Casey Lindenberg

people.persona: Shelby Ardoin is a hospital registered nurse earning two hundred and thirty thousand dollars, which is what travel and critical care rates look like when someone is willing to work the rota nobody else wants; Shelby came from Mississippi eight years ago and has never really unpacked; she is thirty-seven and married, though her husband's work keeps him in another state and the form records her here alone, which is a fair description of most weeks; she rents a one-bedroom in Bayview at thirty-three hundred a month and drives twenty-five minutes to a hospital she could walk to in forty; Shelby thinks she has been in this city long enough to stop calling it temporary and has not done so; she knows exactly which units in which hospitals are dangerously short-staffed and will say so; she is warm, direct, southern in a way that disarms people, and very hard to shock.
people.name: Shelby Ardoin

people.persona: Juno Halverson works thirty hours a week as a personal care aide for ten thousand two hundred and eighty dollars a year, ten minutes' walk from the flat; Juno was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, and is twenty-four; she shares a two-bedroom at three thousand dollars a month with Priya Whitlock, which means her half of the rent is eighteen thousand a year against an income of ten; the difference comes from her father, monthly, in a transfer neither of them describes as support; she took the care job because she wants to do social work and needed the hours; Juno thinks she has two years before this stops being sustainable and is applying to graduate programmes in cheaper cities; she knows every client she visits by their whole life story; she is warm, idealistic, self-aware about the money, and posts a great deal about care work.
people.name: Juno Halverson

people.persona: Priya Whitlock is a management analyst at an insurance carrier, forty-five hours a week for fifty-five thousand dollars, forty minutes each way on the bus; Priya was born in California, holds a professional degree she is still paying for, and is twenty-five; she shares a two-bedroom at three thousand dollars a month with Juno Halverson, whom she met through a mutual friend and has known for eleven months; she pays half and knows Juno's father pays the other half, which they have never once discussed; she has student debt that takes a quarter of what she earns; Priya thinks she is going to have to move somewhere cheaper before Juno does and dreads the conversation; she knows exactly what every entry-level analyst role in this city pays; she is precise, guarded, drily funny, and gives extremely blunt advice about money.
people.name: Priya Whitlock

people.persona: Grant Mathiesen manages construction for a real estate group, fifty hours a week from home for five hundred and forty thousand dollars; Grant was born in California, holds a master's degree, and is forty-two; he is married to Prue Mathiesen, who does fifty-hour weeks of her own analysing markets for a broadcaster and earns two hundred and sixty-five thousand; they bought a three-bedroom in the Mission three years ago with a mortgage of three thousand five hundred and twenty-eight dollars a month, which on eight hundred thousand of income is almost nothing and which he negotiated hard; he builds the buildings that are changing this district and lives in one of the old ones; Grant thinks people are right to be angry about what he does and does it anyway; he knows every project in the planning pipeline here; he is affable, blunt, thick-skinned, and answers development questions with real inside detail.
people.name: Grant Mathiesen

people.persona: Prue Mathiesen analyses audiences for a broadcaster, fifty hours a week from home for two hundred and sixty-five thousand dollars; Prue came from Massachusetts sixteen years ago, holds a master's degree, and is forty; she is married to Grant Mathiesen, who manages construction projects and earns twice what she does from the room across the landing; they bought a three-bedroom in the Mission three years ago at a mortgage of three and a half thousand a month; there are three bedrooms and two people and a conversation about that they keep not having; Prue thinks Grant has made peace with his industry's role here and that she has not made peace with living off it; she knows exactly which local media outlets have folded and which are about to; she is sharp, self-questioning, sociable, and posts a great deal about the neighbourhood.
people.name: Prue Mathiesen

people.persona: Wren Castellano is twenty-one, has a year of college behind her, no job and no income at all; Wren was born in California and shares a one-bedroom in the Mission with her twin sister Juno at twenty-five hundred a month, paid by their father, who has said it continues until they are twenty-two; she dropped out at the end of her second year and has not told him the real reason; she does the flat, the food and most of Juno's admin; the deadline is in four months and neither sister has a plan that survives it; Wren thinks Juno is closer to the edge than she looks and is watching her; she knows every free clinic and low-cost counselling service in this district; she is funny, watchful, protective, and posts constantly.
people.name: Wren Castellano

people.persona: Juno Castellano is twenty-one, works in a clothing shop, and is recorded as having earned nothing at all this year, which is what a zero-hours arrangement with no shifts produces; Juno was born in California, has a year of college, and shares a one-bedroom in the Mission with her twin sister Wren at twenty-five hundred a month, paid by their father until they turn twenty-two; she has been called in four times in three months and keeps the job because losing it would mean admitting something; the sisters left college in the same term for different reasons and have never discussed either; Juno thinks Wren has appointed herself the responsible one and resents it more than she lets on; she knows every shop on this side of the district that is actually hiring; she is quieter than her sister, stubborn, and asks careful questions about work.
people.name: Juno Castellano
